event_confirmation: Company release 2026-10-12: Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-22 after market close, call 5:00 pm ET. https://www.bloomenergy.com/news/bloom-energy-to-announce-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-on-october-22-2026/
conviction_note: abs_move 11.5 (front straddle 10.16%, prints of +27/+18% in the last four, likely 2027 and bookings commentary, the session already -10.7% intraday) times a slight lean up, p_up 54: the bar ($1.05-1.07B revenue, flat q/q) sits at the low end of what the raised FY guide implies for H2, estimates have only gone up, and the stock has lost 23% in 20 days, mostly in sector risk-off. Against that, a 30% Q2 revenue beat with a raised guide closed -1.85%, and Jupiter/Oracle is a live negative on the guidance line. The findings sum to +0.9 and the scaled number is +0.92; they agree by coincidence, not by fitting.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $1.05-1.07B and non-GAAP EPS $0.67-0.71: MarketBeat $1.07B / $0.69 (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-22-bloom-energy-co-stock/), Seeking Alpha preview $1.07B / $0.67 (https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:c7e3e76f0094b:0-bloom-energy-s-q3-results-to-test-ai-driven-growth-expectations/), Benzinga $1.05B / $0.68, Zacks $0.71. FY2026 company guide (raised 2026-07-28): revenue $3.9-4.2B, non-GAAP GM ~34%, non-GAAP op income $800-900M, non-GAAP EPS $2.55-2.85 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001664703/000162828026050150/ex991_q226financialresults.htm). H1 revenue was $1,816.4M ($751.1M + $1,065.4M), so the guide implies H2 of $2.08-2.38B, or $1.04-1.19B a quarter. The bar is sourced to two or more agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest 20.98M shares, 7.25% of float, days to cover 1.22, up from 19.21M a month earlier (stockanalysis.com, page updated 2026-10-22, settlement date not shown: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/be/statistics/). That is not a crowded short. Skew is +2.06 vol points, meaning downside is paid mildly, and the put/call OI ratio is 0.82. The front straddle implies 10.16%. The stock is -22.72% over 20 days, -11.14% over 5 days and -38.5% from its 52-week high. On the day of the print it traded -10.7% intraday ($212.89 at 13:49 ET) in a broad AI-infrastructure sell-off: Nasdaq-100 -2.9%, FCEL about -9.6%, chipmakers -7-8%. It joined the S&P 500 on 2026-09-21, so index buying is done. The name is retail-heavy: Hunterbrook disclosed a short in July 2026.

findings.finding: The consensus Q3 revenue bar ($1.05-1.07B) is flat on Q2 ($1,065.4M) and at the bottom of what the raised FY guide implies. H1 was $1,816.4M, so $3.9-4.2B needs H2 of $2.08-2.38B, or $1.04-1.19B a quarter. Bloom beat Q2 revenue by about 30% ($1,065M vs about $823M expected) and EPS by 2x ($0.78 vs $0.39), and has beaten 7 of its last 8 quarters. Q3 EPS estimates have had 17 upward revisions and none down in three months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-28): a ~30% revenue beat and a raised FY guide went +12% after hours, then closed the window -1.85% (baseline). Q1 2026 (2026-04-28): a beat and raise moved +27.21%. Q3 2025: +18.03%. So this name has both paid and sold the beat line; the most recent one was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is visibly conservative against the company's own H2 arithmetic: consensus models Q3 EPS down 14% q/q. If a beat were priced, the stock would not be -23% over 20 days into the print and -10.7% on the day, and the preview copy would not frame the print as a test of whether Bloom can keep its growth.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001664703/000162828026027913/ex991_q126financialresults.htm) gives Q1 revenue of $751.1M, used for the H1 arithmetic. The estimate history comes from the Seeking Alpha preview (https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:c7e3e76f0094b:0-bloom-energy-s-q3-results-to-test-ai-driven-growth-expectations/). Both rest on the same company guide.

findings.finding: The corrected 10-Q/A (filed 2026-07-29) shows that one non-related customer was ~73% of Q2 revenue (about $780M), and that related-party revenue fell from $373M in Q1 to $2.8M in Q2. Quarterly revenue therefore rides on one or two very large deliveries; the CFO said 'one or two customers could lead our revenue in any given quarter.' If Q3 lacks a delivery of Q2's size, it can come in below a bar that was set off Q2's level.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The Q2 concentration was not disclosed until the 10-Q, and the Q2 beat was sold anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: The figure sits in a 10-Q/A explanatory-note correction, not in the release or in any preview. Previews model Q3 as flat q/q as if Q2 were a run rate. Net of the rest of the company: management said it raised the FY guide on 'visibility and confidence for our second half' and that guidance has no dependence on any single project, so the downside is bounded. That is why the size is small and the range wide.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript, CFO on concentration and delivery timing (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-bloom-energy-tops-q2-2026-forecasts-shares-jump-after-hours-93CH-4818294). This partly argues the other way, since the concentration is timing rather than backlog composition.

findings.finding: Bloom's largest named project, Oracle's 2.45 GW Project Jupiter, is slipping. Oracle sent a force majeure notice on 2026-09-24. The Energy Transfer gas pipeline is delayed about six months, to 2027-02-01. The air permit is stalled: an NMED email of 2026-10-09 discusses an extension past the 2026-11-23 decision deadline, a motion to dismiss the application is pending, and Oracle/YGI will propose a design change to cut emissions 35%. Expect pressure on the guidance and 2027 lines in the call Q&A.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The force majeure headline on 2026-09-24 coincided with BE -8% that day (247wallst timeline; Treasury yields were also cited). No print has yet reacted to a project delay.
findings.why_not_priced: The force majeure is widely known and partly priced: an Investing.com piece of 2026-10-12 names it as an overhang. The later local-press detail is not in wire previews: the permit-extension email, the motion to dismiss and the 35% emissions-cut redesign, which could change the fuel-cell scope. Net of the rest: the Oracle partnership is up to 2.8 GW, AEP/Google, Aligned and Brookfield ($25B framework) are separate, and management says the guide is not single-project dependent. Hence the modest size.
findings.independence: TechCrunch on the force majeure (https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/24/oracle-sends-force-majeure-notice-on-its-new-mexico-stargate-data-center/). ENR/BigGo summaries give the pipeline delay to 2027-02-01. These are a different outlet and document from the ABQ Journal source.

findings.finding: A counterparty disclosed a new Bloom project not yet announced by Bloom. LS Electric announced on 2026-10-13 a $138.5M (KRW 185.3bn) Bloom order for 38 kV switchgear and transformers for a Pennsylvania data-center fuel-cell project, delivering April-July 2027. That takes cumulative Bloom orders to LS above $500M since April 2025; its April order of $216.5M was for the 2.45 GW New Mexico site. The site is likely Aligned's 2 GW Project Phoenix (RBC, 2026-09-15), which points to a large 2027 deployment that can show up as bookings or backlog on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bloom reports backlog annually ($6B entering 2026, +140%). Bookings and capacity announcements drove the +27% (Q1 2026) and +18% (Q3 2025) reactions; the baseline holds the move sizes, the attribution is the sweep's.
findings.why_not_priced: Bloom has issued no release on Pennsylvania or Phoenix; its newsroom since July carries sponsorships and product items only. On the day of the LS disclosure BE fell 9.3%, which Slicast attributes to no catalyst. If the market were carrying a firm 2 GW 2027 booking, the stock would not be at -38% from its high with flat-q/q estimates. Phoenix was public via an RBC note on 2026-09-15, so this is partly known.
findings.independence: RBC's 'meaningful proof point' note on Phoenix (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/bloom-energy-gains-another-meaningful-proof-point-with-project-phoenix-says-rbc-2-gw-build-reinforces-data-center-opportunity/cZtnKFhRBcp). This is a different source; the link between the LS order and Phoenix is reported as likely, not confirmed.

findings.finding: AEP announced on 2026-10-14 a ~$4B, 702 MW Cheyenne, Wyoming fuel-cell project using Bloom fuel cells under its previously announced up-to-1 GW agreement. Google signed a 20-year PPA, construction starts in 2026, and it is fully operational by end-2028. Existing backlog now has a named hyperscaler offtaker and a schedule.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print isolates this line. The AEP 1 GW agreement was announced earlier and is in backlog.
findings.why_not_priced: The project lands inside an already-announced agreement, so the dollars are not new; what is new is the firm offtaker and timeline, which de-risks conversion. The stock fell over the following week, so the market did not pay for it.
findings.independence: The BigGo preview of 2026-10-19 (https://finance.biggo.com/news/2e066f36-6b46-40e3-91a5-7f93272ccf3a) repeats it. Same underlying AEP release.

findings.finding: Bloom's anchor partner Oracle (up to 2.8 GW) is under financing strain. ORCL was $123.75, -4.2% on 2026-10-22. On 2026-10-12, OpenAI, its largest cloud customer, reportedly disclosed annualized revenue about $20B below estimates, and Oracle is in talks with Apollo/Goldman to finance chips off balance sheet. Analysts can be expected to press for Oracle order timing and bookings on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on a print. BE has traded with ORCL and AI-infrastructure risk-off through July-October.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: BE is -23% in 20 days alongside ORCL. It is filed small because it is macro-to-company transmission that neither Bloom nor Oracle has confirmed affects Bloom orders. Oracle says Jupiter 'remains on our planned schedule'.
findings.independence: Proxy. The ORCL price comes from the Motley Fool page of 2026-10-20 (https://fool.com/investing/2026/10/20/bloom-energy-vs-oracle-which-ai-infrastructure-sto). It shares the Oracle theme with the Jupiter finding but rests on a different fact (Oracle's balance sheet, not the site).

findings.finding: Pre-print de-risking has already happened. BE is -22.7% over 20 days, -11.1% over 5 days and -10.7% intraday on print day ($212.89, reversing a +7% on 2026-10-21) in a sector sell-off (Nasdaq-100 -2.9%, FCEL -9.6%, chipmakers -7-8%) with no company news. Short interest is a modest 7.25% of float (1.2 days to cover), and the S&P 500 inclusion buying (2026-09-21) is behind it. A reasonable print meets lowered positioning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: -11.3% on print day (close $166.84), then a beat; the window closed -1.85%. So a pre-print flush did not guarantee a bounce last time.
findings.why_not_priced: Today's drop is attributed to tech and chip weakness and pre-earnings caution, not company news. The skew is only +2.06, so the option market is not paying heavily for further downside. If the market held a company-specific negative, the skew would be steeper and short interest rising sharply.
findings.independence: The Motley Fool quote at 13:49 ET (https://fool.com/investing/2026/10/20/bloom-energy-vs-oracle-which-ai-infrastructure-sto) and stockanalysis short interest (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/be/statistics/) are different sources.

findings.finding: Insiders kept selling into the run. EDGAR shows Form 144 notices on 2026-08-13/14/17, four on 2026-09-16 and one on 2026-10-01, each followed by Form 4s. Amounts and 10b5-1 status were not checked.
findings.why_not_priced: The filings are public and routine for this name. Filed small for completeness: a judge may read the cluster as signal or as plan sales.

baseline_tension: The slight up-lean runs against the mild put skew (+2.06) and against momentum (-23% over 20 days, -10.7% on print day). It agrees with a sell-off that is sector-wide rather than company-specific, and with a not-crowded short. The tension is why p_up is only 54.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q2 30% beat and raise closed -1.85%, so the bar-beat finding was cut from +1.5 to +0.8 and p_up moved from 55 to 54.

Lesson 9 (net of the rest of the company): the Jupiter finding was cut from -1.5 to -1.0 because the Oracle partnership is up to 2.8 GW alongside AEP, Aligned and Brookfield, and management says the guide does not depend on one project.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed small): the Oracle financing-strain finding was cut from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 3 (resolve your own caveat): the concentration finding argues both ways, so it was cut from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lessons 6 and 7 left the rest standing: the bar is sourced, the Oct 26 hearing and the Nov 23 permit deadline were already in outside_window, and short interest was checked and is not crowded.
